verdict.rationale: Both fix the root cause, CRM records keyed by `customer_id`, and both route the export through `requireCustomer`, so unknown customers fail cleanly as the README requires. B converts CRM records where they are loaded in `sources.js`, which keeps `buildCustomerIndex` unchanged and leaves its existing tests untouched. A puts source-specific key handling into the domain index and has to weaken three existing identity assertions to `deepEqual`. B also adds a test for the new unknown-customer behavior of the export, which A leaves untested, and B's report honestly flags the remaining risk of duplicate ids.
a_issues: Puts CRM-specific key handling into `buildCustomerIndex`, which mixes source-format concerns into the domain index and accepts either key from any source.
Changes three existing assertions from `equal` to `deepEqual`, weakening tests that previously checked the index returns the original record.
No test covers the new `requireCustomer` behavior in `exportInvoices` (unknown customer gives `UnknownReferenceError` naming the invoice).
The normalized copy keeps the stray `customer_id` field alongside `customerId`.
b_issues: The new `requireCustomer` import is placed out of alphabetical order before `csv.js`, a minor style nit.
If an id appeared in both systems, the CRM record would silently override the billing one; this is noted in the report but not handled.

verdict.rationale: Both changes fix the crash by reconciling the CRM `customer_id` key and switching the export to `requireCustomer`, which follows the README rule on unknown references. A maps CRM records to `customerId` where they are loaded in `sources.js`, so the domain index keeps a single schema and `buildCustomerIndex` behaves as before. B puts a `customerId ?? customer_id` fallback into `buildCustomerIndex` and stores copies of each record, which changes object identity and forced three existing test assertions to be loosened. A also tests the new unknown-customer path in the export, and its report points out the remaining risk of the same id appearing in both systems.
a_issues: New import of customers.js is placed before csv.js, breaking the alphabetical order of the imports (cosmetic)
Does not detect duplicate customer ids across billing and CRM, though the report says so
b_issues: Normalizes the CRM schema inside the domain function `buildCustomerIndex` instead of where the data is loaded, so both key spellings leak into core code
The index now stores copies instead of the original records, which changes behavior and required loosening three existing assertions from `equal` to `deepEqual`
No test covers the new `requireCustomer` error path in `exportInvoices`
Does not mention the risk of duplicate ids across the two systems
